raw_response:
I been farming this land 30 years, my father farmed it before me. I do same thing every year mostly, only change a little if last year was bad or if neighbors got better harvest with something different.

My 10.9 mu — I split it. About 7 mu I do wheat then maize, one after the other, that is the way everyone here does it. The other 3.9 mu I plant cotton in spring. Cotton takes the whole season so cannot do wheat after.

For wheat I plant in October. I use the same seed I bought from the dealer in town — neighbor Wang got 900 jin per mu with it last year so I trust it. Before planting I spread 2 bags of compound fertilizer per mu, that is the 15-15-15 kind, plus 1 bag of urea. Then in spring when wheat starts standing up I broadcast another half bag of urea per mu when I irrigate. I water 4 times — once before winter, then jointing, then when ear comes out, then when grain filling. If I water less the grain stays small, I saw it happen to my cousin.

For maize after wheat I just rotary till and plant right away, no time to waste. I use the hybrid seed everyone uses, the dealer tells me which one. I put 2 bags of compound fertilizer in the row when planting and side-dress 1 bag of urea when maize is knee-high. Water 2 times if rain is short. Spray for the borer 2 times.

Cotton is the most work. I plough it deep before planting because cotton roots go down. I use 2 bags compound, 1 bag urea base, then more urea later. Cotton needs spraying many times for the bollworm, I spray maybe 6 times through summer, cannot skip or whole crop is lost. I irrigate 3 times.

I would rather spend a little extra on fertilizer than have a bad harvest. Money on fertilizer is just cost, bad harvest is disaster for my family.
